S — Synthetic modern coding; DSM-5-TR severe alcohol use disorder maps to F10.20 when withdrawal is coded separately. Person-first language; not a claim about her real diagnosis.
Alcohol withdrawal, mild, at low risk of complications (PAWSS 3, CIWA-Ar 9 at intake; no past seizures or delirium tremens), managed as an outpatient with daily nurse checks
S — Synthetic withdrawal episode; resolved by the one-week visit.
Raised liver enzymes (AST 96, ALT 44, GGT 240 U/L) with a FIB-4 index of 3.93, above the cut point for possible advanced fibrosis; liver stiffness measurement planned
S — Synthetic presenting finding; superseded when elastography and the clinical picture supported alcohol-associated steatotic liver disease.
Depressive symptoms during heavy drinking (PHQ-9 14, item 9 scored 0); whether they are alcohol-induced or an independent depression to be judged after two to four weeks without alcohol
S — Synthetic provisional finding; resolved as the PHQ-9 fell to 5 after ten weeks without alcohol, consistent with alcohol-induced depressive symptoms. Not a claim about her real mood.

list.item: Alcohol use disorder, severe (nine of eleven DSM-5-TR criteria), daily drinking of about a pint of whiskey with heavier binges for many years; synthetic modern episode linked to her documented lifelong heavy drinking: active, confirmed [S]
Alcohol withdrawal, mild, at low risk of complications (PAWSS 3, CIWA-Ar 9 at intake; no past seizures or delirium tremens), managed as an outpatient with daily nurse checks: active, confirmed [S]
Raised liver enzymes (AST 96, ALT 44, GGT 240 U/L) with a FIB-4 index of 3.93, above the cut point for possible advanced fibrosis; liver stiffness measurement planned: active, confirmed [S]

Depressive symptoms during heavy drinking (PHQ-9 14, item 9 scored 0); whether they are alcohol-induced or an independent depression to be judged after two to four weeks without alcohol: active, provisional [S]
Daily chewing tobacco for many years; not ready to stop at intake: active, confirmed [S]
Underweight (BMI 18.4) with poor food intake, low folate, magnesium and phosphate, and slightly low albumin: active, confirmed [S]
Housing instability: staying in a spare room at a friend's house, with nowhere to go if that ends; has stayed in shelters in past winters: active, confirmed [S]
Food insecurity: often goes without meals at the end of the month: active, confirmed [S]

A nonjudgmental, trauma-informed assessment: AUDIT, DSM-5-TR criteria and PEth explained as part of care, person-first language, a female clinician and a chaperone offered, consent asked before each part of the examination, and her own goals and choices first. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); The Healthcare Professional's Core Resource on Alcohol (2026); Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (2018) [S]

Addiction medicine consultation to confirm the diagnosis, review withdrawal and choose a medicine for alcohol use disorder. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management (2020) [S]

Outpatient withdrawal management at low risk (PAWSS 3, CIWA-Ar 9): a five-day gabapentin schedule, daily nurse checks with the CIWA-Ar in person or by the clinic phone, her friend as support, fluids and food; hospital care at once for a CIWA-Ar of 15 or more, a seizure, hallucinations, confusion or vomiting. Guideline: The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management (2020) [S]

Thiamine 100 mg by injection for three days, then by mouth, with folic acid, potassium and magnesium replacement. Guideline: The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management (2020); Diagnosis and Treatment of Alcohol-Associated Liver Diseases: 2019 Practice Guidance From the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (2019) [S]

Liver: FIB-4 of 3.93, so transient elastography; liver enzymes, albumin, INR and platelets followed; hepatitis A and B vaccination; acetaminophen no more than 2 g a day. Guideline: Diagnosis and Treatment of Alcohol-Associated Liver Diseases: 2019 Practice Guidance From the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (2019) [S]

Mood and safety: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 again after two to four weeks without alcohol before deciding on depression treatment; a structured safety assessment, a written safety plan, the rifle stored with her friend, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monograph (2026) [S]

Recovery support and harm reduction: weekly contact with the clinic's peer recovery support specialist, her choice of mutual-help meetings (Alcoholics Anonymous, SMART Recovery or Women for Sobriety), and a plan for a return to drinking: call the peer specialist or the clinic, eat, do not drink alone or drive, keep taking any medicine for alcohol use disorder, and come back without shame. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); The Healthcare Professional's Core Resource on Alcohol (2026) [S]

Housing, food, income and coverage: the clinic's community health worker helps with a Montana Medicaid application, SNAP benefits, a food bank, the local Human Resource Development Council's housing programs, Montana 211, and a free phone through the Lifeline program. Guideline: The Healthcare Professional's Core Resource on Alcohol (2026) [S]

Alcohol and women's health: why the same amount of alcohol does women more harm (higher blood alcohol, faster liver damage, a higher breast cancer risk), a pregnancy test, contraception if needed, and breast and cervical cancer screening at the preventive visit. Guideline: The Healthcare Professional's Core Resource on Alcohol (2026) [S]
Chewing tobacco: advice to stop and nicotine replacement offered whenever she is ready. Guideline: Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Including Pregnant Persons: Interventions (2021) [S]
